I'm mapping out the branches to test in this class—checking whether read() hits end-of-stream versus successfully returning a byte, and similarly for the array-based read variants, skip, and getValue.

I'll use CRC32 with ByteArrayInputStream for realistic behavior, adding mocked InputStreams where needed to test exception propagation. I'm planning out specific test cases covering normal reads, EOF cases, partial reads, skip behavior on data vs EOF, and checksum value verification.

I also want to check edge cases like null byte arrays and zero-length reads, plus use Mockito to verify exact checksum.update() interactions alongside real stream tests for correctness.

For the read(byte[], off, len) tests, I plan to cover partial reads and mismatches, and I'll mock the underlying stream to isolate the skip() logic since skip relies on read() internally.

For IOException propagation, I'll mock InputStream.read() to throw and confirm it bubbles up through both read() variants. I also want to test the null-checksum constructor case—since the constructor doesn't validate, passing null should cause a NullPointerException later when checksum.update() gets invoked during a real read, so I'll write a test that expects that exception.

Now I'll assemble the final test code along with a summary table in Thai.
